title: Union-literal convergence: predicates, type guards, leaf vocabulary, display mirrors
summary: How to burn down union-literal branches onto canonical projections without breaking narrowing, imports, or the client/server module boundary.
hint_triggers: Burning down union-literal branches: (1) convert comparisons to owner-module predicates; use `x is Extract<U,{kind:K}>` type guards (or generic `C & {kind:K}`) wherever the caller consumes narrowed members, plain booleans only when no narrowing is needed. (2) Prefer Record-typed tables keyed by the union member for fan-out logic. (3) When a predicate creates an import cycle, sink the union vocabulary + predicates to a leaf module both sides import. (4) Client components cannot import server-dep core modules — keep display-side canonical mirrors and let the gate baseline them as owner-adjacent. (5) Never register an inline union whose sibling literals collide with other domains; use a structural discriminator field instead. (6) After moving or adding predicate definitions, regenerate the shrink-only baseline with --write-baseline rather than hand-editing it.
